title: Ions, salts and electrolytes

concepts.label: ionic bond
concepts.definition: The electric (Coulomb) attraction between a cation and an anion; it grows with the charges and falls with the square of the distance.

concepts.label: crystal lattice (salt)
concepts.definition: The regular repeating arrangement in which every ion is surrounded by ions of opposite sign (6 neighbours in NaCl); a substance built this way is a salt, and it has no separate cation–anion pairs.

concepts.label: ionic formula (charge balance)
concepts.definition: The smallest whole-number ratio of cations to anions whose charges sum to zero, written cation first with counts as subscripts: NaCl, MgCl2, Al2O3.

concepts.label: polyatomic ion
concepts.definition: A tightly bound group of atoms that carries a net charge and behaves as one ion: sulfate SO4 2−, hydroxide OH−, nitrate NO3−; brackets mark more than one in a formula, e.g. Ca(OH)2.

concepts.label: mole
concepts.definition: A counting unit of 6.022 × 10^23 particles (atoms, ions or formula units), chosen so that a mole of an element weighs its periodic-table mass in grams.

concepts.label: molar mass
concepts.definition: The mass of one mole of a substance in g/mol, the sum of the atomic masses in its formula (NaCl: 58.44 g/mol); moles = grams / molar mass.

concepts.label: polar water molecule
concepts.definition: H2O is a neutral molecule (a bound group of atoms) whose oxygen end is slightly negative and hydrogen ends slightly positive, so it is attracted to ions of either sign.

concepts.label: dissociation
concepts.definition: A salt's lattice coming apart in water into separate, freely moving, water-wrapped cations and anions in the ratio of its formula, e.g. MgCl2(s) → Mg2+(aq) + 2Cl−(aq).

concepts.label: concentration (mol/L)
concepts.definition: Moles of dissolved substance per litre of solution; written with square brackets for a single ion, e.g. [Cl−] = 0.2 mol/L.

concepts.label: ionic vs electronic conduction
concepts.definition: In metals current is carried by moving electrons while the atoms stay put; in liquids containing ions it is carried by the ions themselves, cations toward the negative plate and anions toward the positive plate.

concepts.label: electrolyte
concepts.definition: A substance that conducts electricity because it contains mobile ions, such as a salt solution or a molten salt (a dry salt crystal is not one: its ions cannot move).

namedOnly: Coulomb's law (stated as force ∝ charge × charge / distance², not used quantitatively afterwards)
covalent / shared-electron bonding inside polyatomic ions and water (pointer to Silicon and light)
solution, saturated solution, (s) and (aq) state symbols (used as plain vocabulary)
conductivity in S/m and the 100 Ω bulb model in the capstone (resistance is taught in Real batteries)
what happens at the plate surface (pointer to Oxidation and reduction and Electrolysis)
1 mol/L as the standard reference concentration (pointer forward)
Cu2+ and Zn2+ as the common ions of copper and zinc (taken as given)
summary: Running example: the Na+ and Cl− made in the first two lessons, followed from a single attracting pair to the NaCl lattice, its formula, a weighed-out mole, a dissolved 0.5 mol/L solution and finally a current-carrying electrolyte; MgCl2, Al2O3, CuSO4 and Ca(OH)2 extend each idea. The capstone is a conductivity tester (battery, bulb, two plates) where the learner picks dry salt, water, NaCl/KNO3/MgCl2/NaOH solutions at 0.0001–1 mol/L, molten NaCl or a copper bar and watches electrons move in the wire and ions between the plates. Later lessons can reuse: CuSO4 and ZnSO4 as dissociated salts, [ion] notation and mol/L, moles = grams / molar mass, and the picture 'electrons in the metal, ions in the electrolyte' with cations drifting to the negative plate.
